units.translation: then, so, in that case (enclitic particle from ἄρα)

enclitic particle formed from ἄρα, which the grammarians cited in the Thesaurus vol. 6 p. 2312 explain by δή; on this see Apollonius in Bekker's Anecdota p. 525, 16. Its use is very frequent among the epic poets, not rare in lyric poetry, but very rare among the tragedians.
There is one example in Aeschylus.
three in Sophocles.
Does the king hear me?
Did Artemis urge you against the herds of cattle belonging to the whole people, or for the sake of some victory without fruit, or deceived in glorious spoils?
Does he insult my dark-faced heart?

rod, staff

rod, staff. For ῥαβδούχος [rod-bearer], which is said to produce words equal to great thoughts and ideas. It is clear that in such places the two words are to be pronounced as one with the letter p doubled, like μεγαρράκος, ὑπορράχιν, ταρρήματα and the rest. But where the meter either allows or requires a short syllable, the short vowel before the letter p remains short, as in Aeschylus Pr. 713 χρίμπτουσα ῥαχίαισιν ἐκπερᾶν χθόνα [grazing the rocky shores to cross the land]. 390 ἐπώνυμόν τε ῥεῦμα καὶ πετρηρεφή [and the stream that gives its name and the rocky roof]. 902 πρὸς ταῦτα ῥιπτέσθω μὲν αἰθαλοῦσσα φλόξ [against these let the smoky flame be hurled]. Eum. 232 ἐγὼ δ᾽ ἀρήξω τὸν ἱκέτην τε ῥύσομαι [I will help and protect the suppliant], and in Sophocles OR. 72 δρῶν ἢ τί φωνῶν τήνδε ῥυσαίμην πόλιν [by doing or saying what could I save this city]. For Dawes, Gaisford and others believed with remarkable error that the short vowel before the letter p is always lengthened, so that poets who shortened it must be thought to have violated a rule that never existed, or the reading transmitted in the manuscripts must be corrected, as at OR. 72, where Hermann, on the basis of a slight error in some copy, τήνδ᾽ ἐρυσαίμην (as in L the scribe had first written τήνδ᾽ ἐρυσάμην, from which a later hand made τήνδε ῥυσαίμην), used the futile conjecture τήνδε γ᾽ ἐρυσαίμην, while others no more wisely conjectured τήνδε λυσαίμην. It can also mean herald or temple servant, as it seems.
where the corrector in M wrote in the margin οἶμαι ἢ Ἑρμοῦ ῥάβδον [I think either the staff of Hermes], which is his own conjecture. Schuetz conjectured ἱερόραβδον [holy staff].
